messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Fwd: Renjin Open Source Development - dplyr package
parts:
Hi Alex,

Copying the mailing list as I think this is generally helpful.

Great! I've added libboost-dev to our renjin-package-builder VM image, but it looks like the version that ships with Ubuntu 14, which the build servers are running, has an older version of Boost:
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/dplyr/0.5.0/build/190

I get the same results you do my laptop with Ubuntu 16.

It also looks like the output of dplyr's native sources include an inline assembly node, which I hadn't encountered before. I've added it to the AST definition as well as stub to just throw an Exception at runtime. We can see later if it's critical to the package or not and then how to handle it.

After fixing this, there appear to be a number of problems compilingon Renjin's side. I fixed a few but I didn't have time to go through them all. The branch is here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/tree/wip-dplyr

The next thing to fix is something called offset types, which I gather is used by GCC to represent C pointers-to-members.... Will require some digging to figure just what the heck this is, but should be reasonable to implement. Let me know if you get stuck!

Best,
Alex



 

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: S. Alex Szebenyi <als...@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, Jun 5, 2017 at 7:49 PM
Subject: Re: Renjin Open Source Development - dplyr package
To: Alexander Bertram <al...@bedatadriven.com>


Hi Alex,

I ran the following apt-gets before building renjin-dplyr:

```

sudo apt-get install make gcc-4.7 gcc-4.7-plugin-dev gfortran-4.7 g++-4.7 gcc-4.7.multilib g++-4.7-multilib

sudo apt-get install libboost-dev

```

I am hitting a new build failure, but it looks like the error message is helpful:

[ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.renjin:renjin-maven-plugin:0.9.0-SNAPSHOT:gnur-compile (compile) on project dplyr: Compilation of GNU R sources failed: Failed to parse gimple file /home/ubuntu/renjin2/dplyr_0.5.0-b189/src/dplyr.gimple: Could not resolve type id 'gimple_asm' into a subtype of [simple type, class org.renjin.gcc.gimple.statement.GimpleStatement]

[ERROR] at [Source: java.io.FileReader@60827a; line: 2023196, column: 15] (through reference chain: org.renjin.gcc.gimple.GimpleCompilationUnit["functions"]->org.renjin.gcc.gimple.GimpleFunction["basicBlocks"]->org.renjin.gcc.gimple.GimpleBasicBlock["statements"])


-------------

Happy to spend some time looking at this although I am not sure where to go from here.


Thank you,

Alex

On Sun, Jun 4, 2017 at 7:54 PM S. Alex Szebenyi <als...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks Alex! 

I really appreciate the reply.  I was able to reproduce the current error 'boost.config.hpp...'  using the link you sent. 

I guess I will probably not need to do this to get you the system packages that need to be installed tofix the build, but I also tried to run the Renjin's maven build via the provided ubuntu vagrant box as described in BUILDING.md.

First it is a very impressive Maven build and I like the that a VM is provided.

I did run into a couple issues with the build:
- Integration tests seemed to fail on master (my host machine is OS X and VM is running on a case sensitive disk image) ; it looked like the JVM died doing something with JNA and could produce a core dump. 
- I ran the build with -DskipTests=true and the build failed on the Renjin Standalone Platform-independent distribution running verify.sh - a few files weren't found

---- 
Running the dplyr build i ran into a problem where the renjin artifacts weren't resolving - they were looking for a 0.8.x beyond what exists in renjin's nexus. I replaced these version numbers in the auto generated pom file with 0.9.0-SNAPSHOT and the build then proceeded to the point where the boost error occured. 
----- 

Let me know if you  want more details/logs/etc.

Anyway, just wanted to give you a progress update, hopefully I'll have figured out those system packages we need to get the dplyr build working soon.

Thank you,
Alex
 


On Sun, Jun 4, 2017 at 8:37 AM, Alexander Bertram <al...@bedatadriven.com> wrote:
Hi Alex!

You're right about the build process -- that's exactly how it works.

We haven't open-sourced the whole system, but there's a link on the page to rebuild a package locally for testing / debugging. The script for the latest build of dplyr is:

curl http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/dplyr/0.5.0/build/189/rebuild.sh | sh

That will download the sources and the auto-generated POM file to a local directory where you can run "mvn install" to rebuild.

Since dplyr includes C/C++ code, you'll need to install the prerequisites for Renjin's native-to-jvm tool chain:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/BUILDING.md

I think the particular issue mentioned in the google groups thread has been resolved, so now it looks like the biggest problem is that that dplyr's native code fails to compile, but only because certain boost libraries aren't available on the build machine. If you can figure out the system packages which need to be installed (for Ubuntu 16) then I'd be happy to add them to the build server configuration.

Let me know if you hit any other problems!

Best,
Alex




On Sun, Jun 4, 2017 at 7:38 AM S. Alex Szebenyi <als...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Alex,

Renjin seems awesome - also BeDataDriven seems like a great company in general. My background has been working on enterprise PaaS and enterprise scale webapps. I know little about R except at a very high level.

I would like to fix up the dplyr package: http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/dplyr/0.5.0

Based on https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/renjin-dev/hG2rCa8tNZg it seemed like you might have some suggestions for a starting point?

I am trying to figure out the process for testing external R packages (e.g., dplyr) I believe I want to execute the following to test a fix: http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/dplyr/0.5.0/build/189


My first guess is that Renjin uses R's system to pull down a given dependency, auto-generates a POM based on the packages metadata, mvn renjin plugin compiles it,  mvn finds any R unit tests and executes those using Renjin and finally deploys generated jar file to renjin's nexus.  

I did not immediately see anything in the documentation about this process although I'm guessing I could find it by digging through the code a little - if there is a doc you could point me to that would be very helpful.

Any help you can offer would be greatly appreciated :).   Renjin is a very cool project and I am enjoying learning more about it. 

Thank you,
Alex Szebenyi

parts:
I'm working on getting the build working in latest master / VM and running into some issues - it seems like the build is passing elsewhere so I'm not sure what is causing the failures. 

A few Integration Tests are failing from the 'tests' module: 
https://github.com/alszeb/renjin/pull/1/commits/79b0b55c65242a53d3a34f84dfba1dba57a58f8f

it looks like 'micro' tests with the eigan function as well as a micro test with a %*% operator are failing.  I commit the commented-out-failing-tests as well as the failure logs for each of those types of cases at the above link. I tried installing `rcppeigan` and  `r-cran-ccpeigan` to the VM although neither of these seemed to help (note that my VM was in a dirty state at the time).

Once those tests are commented out, the build proceeds and I get the following failure:
[ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.renjin:renjin-maven-plugin:0.9.0-SNAPSHOT:gnur-compile (build) on project cran.dot.package: Compilation of GNU R sources failed: Cannot run program "make" (in directory "/home/ubuntu/renjin/test-packages/cran.dot.package/src"): error=2, No such file or directory -> [Help 1]


I want to figure out if its something with my environment or an issue with the VM - has anyone build renjin on a fresh vagrant up of the VM? 

Any ideas on what to check out next?

Thank you,
Alex S.

You're right about the build process -- that's exactly how it works.

We haven't open-sourced the whole system, but there's a link on the page to rebuild a package locally for testing / debugging. The script for the latest build of dplyr is:

curl http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/dplyr/0.5.0/build/189/rebuild.sh | sh

That will download the sources and the auto-generated POM file to a local directory where you can run "mvn install" to rebuild.

Since dplyr includes C/C++ code, you'll need to install the prerequisites for Renjin's native-to-jvm tool chain:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/BUILDING.md

I think the particular issue mentioned in the google groups thread has been resolved, so now it looks like the biggest problem is that that dplyr's native code fails to compile, but only because certain boost libraries aren't available on the build machine. If you can figure out the system packages which need to be installed (for Ubuntu 16) then I'd be happy to add them to the build server configuration.

Let me know if you hit any other problems!

Best,
Alex

Hi Alex,

Renjin seems awesome - also BeDataDriven seems like a great company in general. My background has been working on enterprise PaaS and enterprise scale webapps. I know little about R except at a very high level.

I would like to fix up the dplyr package: http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/dplyr/0.5.0

Based on https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/renjin-dev/hG2rCa8tNZg it seemed like you might have some suggestions for a starting point?

I am trying to figure out the process for testing external R packages (e.g., dplyr) I believe I want to execute the following to test a fix: http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/dplyr/0.5.0/build/189


My first guess is that Renjin uses R's system to pull down a given dependency, auto-generates a POM based on the packages metadata, mvn renjin plugin compiles it,  mvn finds any R unit tests and executes those using Renjin and finally deploys generated jar file to renjin's nexus.  

I did not immediately see anything in the documentation about this process although I'm guessing I could find it by digging through the code a little - if there is a doc you could point me to that would be very helpful.

Any help you can offer would be greatly appreciated :).   Renjin is a very cool project and I am enjoying learning more about it. 

Thank you,
Alex Szebenyi

I'm working on getting the build working in latest master / VM and running into some issues - it seems like the build is passing elsewhere so I'm not sure what is causing the failures. 

A few Integration Tests are failing from the 'tests' module: 
https://github.com/alszeb/renjin/pull/1/commits/79b0b55c65242a53d3a34f84dfba1dba57a58f8f

it looks like 'micro' tests with the eigan function as well as a micro test with a %*% operator are failing.  I commit the commented-out-failing-tests as well as the failure logs for each of those types of cases at the above link. I tried installing `rcppeigan` and  `r-cran-ccpeigan` to the VM although neither of these seemed to help (note that my VM was in a dirty state at the time).

Once those tests are commented out, the build proceeds and I get the following failure:
[ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.renjin:renjin-maven-plugin:0.9.0-SNAPSHOT:gnur-compile (build) on project cran.dot.package: Compilation of GNU R sources failed: Cannot run program "make" (in directory "/home/ubuntu/renjin/test-packages/cran.dot.package/src"): error=2, No such file or directory -> [Help 1]


I want to figure out if its something with my environment or an issue with the VM - has anyone build renjin on a fresh vagrant up of the VM? 

Any ideas on what to check out next?

Thank you,
Alex S.

This was a good read from recent commits: https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/tools/gcc-bridge/docs/Packages.md



On Tue, Jun 6, 2017 at 5:37 PM, Alexander Bertram <al...@bedatadriven.com> wrote:
Hi Alex,

Copying the mailing list as I think this is generally helpful.

Great! I've added libboost-dev to our renjin-package-builder VM image, but it looks like the version that ships with Ubuntu 14, which the build servers are running, has an older version of Boost:
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/dplyr/0.5.0/build/190

I get the same results you do my laptop with Ubuntu 16.

It also looks like the output of dplyr's native sources include an inline assembly node, which I hadn't encountered before. I've added it to the AST definition as well as stub to just throw an Exception at runtime. We can see later if it's critical to the package or not and then how to handle it.

After fixing this, there appear to be a number of problems compilingon Renjin's side. I fixed a few but I didn't have time to go through them all. The branch is here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/tree/wip-dplyr

The next thing to fix is something called offset types, which I gather is used by GCC to represent C pointers-to-members.... Will require some digging to figure just what the heck this is, but should be reasonable to implement. Let me know if you get stuck!

Best,
Alex

On Sun, Jun 4, 2017 at 7:54 PM S. Alex Szebenyi <als...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks Alex! 

I really appreciate the reply.  I was able to reproduce the current error 'boost.config.hpp...'  using the link you sent. 

I guess I will probably not need to do this to get you the system packages that need to be installed tofix the build, but I also tried to run the Renjin's maven build via the provided ubuntu vagrant box as described in BUILDING.md.

First it is a very impressive Maven build and I like the that a VM is provided.

I did run into a couple issues with the build:
- Integration tests seemed to fail on master (my host machine is OS X and VM is running on a case sensitive disk image) ; it looked like the JVM died doing something with JNA and could produce a core dump. 
- I ran the build with -DskipTests=true and the build failed on the Renjin Standalone Platform-independent distribution running verify.sh - a few files weren't found

---- 
Running the dplyr build i ran into a problem where the renjin artifacts weren't resolving - they were looking for a 0.8.x beyond what exists in renjin's nexus. I replaced these version numbers in the auto generated pom file with 0.9.0-SNAPSHOT and the build then proceeded to the point where the boost error occured. 
----- 

Let me know if you  want more details/logs/etc.

Anyway, just wanted to give you a progress update, hopefully I'll have figured out those system packages we need to get the dplyr build working soon.

Thank you,
Alex
